artists.biography:
One of New York’s most notable ska bands, the Slackers formed in Brooklyn in 1991 and have played the world over many times since. Their first release was an eponymous self-released album, distributed by Moon Records in 1993 on cassette. Their first real debut is “Better Late Than Never” on moon ska records. Coming out in 1996, this album saw a movement to more traditional ska music, as opposed to their earlier two-tone and garage influences. It was produced by Victor Rice, a noted ska/reggae producer, who also played bass for them at one point.

Band members are as follows:
Vic Ruggiero - Keyboards, Vocals
Jay “Agent Jay” Nugent - Guitar
Dave Hillyard - Saxophone
Glen Pine - Trombone, Vocals
Marcus Geard - Bass
Ara Babajian - Drums

perplexity.description:
Peculiar" is a 2006 album by The Slackers, a New York City band known for their blend of ska and reggae. Released originally on Hellcat Records, the album showcases the band's signature fusion of traditional reggae rhythms with ska's upbeat energy, enriched by soulful organ, trombone, and saxophone arrangements. The musical style on "Peculiar" is characterized by a laid-back yet rhythmically engaging sound, with Vic Ruggiero's vocals and songwriting at the core, supported by the band's tight instrumentation and occasional guest contributions that add depth and texture to the tracks.

Within The Slackers' discography, "Peculiar" stands as a mature work that reflects their evolution over more than a decade of recording and performing. It follows a series of well-received albums and is often regarded as a highlight for its consistency and the quality of its songwriting. The album received positive critical attention, with reviewers praising its solid composition and the band's ability to maintain freshness within the reggae and ska genres. It has been reissued multiple times, including a notable 2019 re-release by Pirates Press Records, which included various vinyl editions and bonus tracks, underscoring its lasting appeal among fans and collectors.

Though not a major commercial blockbuster, "Peculiar" is respected in the reggae and ska communities for its authentic sound and the band's energetic yet nuanced performances. Its reception solidified The Slackers' reputation as stalwarts of the genre, capable of delivering both danceable grooves and thoughtful lyrics. The album's enduring presence in their catalog and continued reissues reflect its significance as a key entry in their body of work.
